subject: BlueWave: Dedicated reservation questionnaire + proposed next steps
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@bluewavehealth.com>
To: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@bluewavehealth.com
Date: 2026-08-22T15:02:00Z
Subject: Dedicated reserve sizing — initial info request

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the intro call today. BlueWave is formalizing an RFP for an inference reservation to support our clinical-document understanding pipeline. We need a short written questionnaire filled with expected throughput assumptions and a proposed reservation phasing so our procurement and security teams can evaluate cost and SLAs.

High-level asks from our side:
- Expected GA model mix (decoder vs. encoder, common open checkpoints)
- GPU SKUs you recommend for steady-state vs. burst
- Throughput targets expressed as tokens/sec and concurrent requests at p50/p95
- Tail-latency budget (p95/p99) and recommended batching strategy
- Reservation phasing (3-6-12 month ramp) and how burst lanes work

Can you return a completed questionnaire and a one-page phasing proposal by EOD Monday (US time)? Procurement would like clear line items for committed monthly spend and any burst/overage pricing.

Best,
Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Data Platform — BlueWave Health
Attachment: BlueWave_RFP_Scope.docx (doc)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@bluewavehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserve sizing — initial info request

Elena — thanks, and great to meet you on the call. Attaching a compact questionnaire and a draft SKU matrix that maps model classes to recommended GPU families.

Quick clarifying Qs so we fill the form precisely:
- Can you confirm average tokens per request and the median request size? (we often see major divergence between p50 and p95 token counts)
- Expected concurrency during peak hour (or a traffic profile CSV if you have one)
- Any required regional placement constraints (we assume us-east for the proposal unless you say otherwise)
- Compliance requirements beyond standard SOC 2 (e.g., HIPAA BAAs)

We plan to propose a 3-phased reservation: pilot (3mo), scale (months 4-6), steady/commit (months 7-12) with an option to enable a 10-20% burst lane for seasonal demand. The attached workbook includes a sample throughput-to-GPU mapping for your review.

Deliverables I will upload by EOD Monday: filled questionnaire, a CSV with phased monthly committed vCPU/GPU slots, and a short one-page narrative.

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachment: rfi-dedicated-sku-matrix.pdf (pdf); dedicated-questionnaire-fillable.xlsx (spreadsheet)

> Thanks for the intro call today. BlueWave is formalizing an RFP...

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T10:05:00Z
Subject: Internal: BlueWave RFP — GPU mix + throughput mapping

Mina/Olga/Karthik — looping you in on BlueWave. I reviewed their notes from the call (Elena's email below). Steps I recommend:
1) Use a conservative baseline assuming 2.5x the p50 token count for p95 sizing; encourage the customer to provide actual request histograms.
2) Provide two SKU mixes: cost-optimized (A100/RTX9000 class quantized float16 + aggressive KV caching) and latency-optimized (H100 class + smaller batch sizes). Spell out the expected tokens/sec per GPU for each model class.
3) Draft a phased commitment CSV where we show committed GPUs per month and a capped burst lane billed at pay-as-you-go.

I started a CSV with GPU_profiles and tokens_per_sec assumptions and added an example mapping for a 13B decoder vs. 7B encoder. Karthik — can you sanity-check the p95 tail-latency numbers (we want to guarantee <250ms p95 for critical read paths on the latency-optimized mix)?

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
Attachment: bluewave_gpu_profile_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)

On 2026-08-23 Mina wrote:
> Elena — thanks, and great to meet you on the call...

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@bluewavehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@bluewavehealth.com
Date: 2026-08-24T17:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserve sizing — initial info request

Mina, Ben — thanks for the rapid turnaround and helpful attachments. Procurement confirmed they prefer a clear 6-month phased commit (pilot + scale) with explicit line items for committed monthly spend and a 15% capped burst lane.

We completed the traffic profile you requested and attached it here — median tokens 40, p95 tokens 330, peak concurrency 220 at UTC-5 10:00-12:00. For compliance: BAAs required (HIPAA).

Please update the workbook with two proposed SKU mixes as Ben suggested and return a one-page phasing proposal and a DocuSign link (we will circulate to procurement once numbers are firm). Also include a quick note on how fallbacks work if a reserved SKU is unavailable (preferred behavior: automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant in a higher family with pre-agreed latency windows).

Target: updated deliverables by Thursday EOD; procurement will judge pricing vs. other vendors.

Regards,
Elena
Attachment: bluewave_traffic_profile_aug2026.csv (csv)
